steps.what: Read the home programs and equipment notes
Instruct patients and families in living skills
Correct the adaptive equipment attempt in the room
Answer families on care of adaptive equipment

tasks.design: She reads the home programs and equipment notes already in the patient dossier in {OTHER}, then instructs the patient and family in the room. Showing the skill, correcting the attempt and answering their questions stay with the occupational therapy assistant. No draft is produced for this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: The instruction is a demonstration with the family, and a written aid would not show the skill.
tasks.enabler_now: No enabler removes the need to instruct patients and families in person.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing whether the family can use the adaptive equipment at home stays with her.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell that a correct demonstration still left the family unsure.
tasks.altitude: Nothing in the week changes. She still reads the programs and instructs in the room.

reach.task: Set the home program the assistant will teach
reach.learn: Which equipment steps the family must see, and which steps she must not change

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: instructing patients and families in home programs, living skills and adaptive equipment is in-person demonstration. The digest products cover intake reports, reminders and billing, not this instruction.

assumptions: The occupational therapist writes the home programs. The assistant reads them in the patient dossier in {OTHER} and does not create the program.
No tool is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
Spoken instruction of the family is not a message sent outside the organisation.
unknowns: Whether families already hold a written home program, or only hear the instruction in the room.
research_questions: Which equipment steps fail most often once the family is home?

already_counted.description: Reading the programs, instructing, correcting the attempt and answering questions stay in a1, a2, a3 and a4.

incremental.description: No tool is added, so there is no upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Instruction, correction and family questions stay in the room, so no hour moves.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Set a calm attitude toward clients
Encourage clients through their treatment programs
Promote a steadier attitude when effort drops

tasks.design: She keeps a positive attitude toward clients by how she speaks and encourages during the treatment programs. No record is added. The attitude is the work, and it stays with the occupational therapy assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attitude is read from the person in the room, not from a form.
tasks.enabler_now: No enabler replaces encouraging a client through a hard moment.
tasks.still_hard: Noticing a drop in attitude, and choosing whether to push or pause, stays with her.
tasks.human_edge: She can feel that a cheerful tone is wrong for this client today.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still sets the tone and promotes a steadier attitude in the room.

reach.task: Encourage a patient through a difficult session
reach.learn: When a drop in attitude means stop rather than push

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: promoting a client's attitude during treatment is in-person encouragement. No digest source measures or automates that encouragement.

assumptions: The treatment program is already set by the occupational therapist. This task is her manner with the client, not a change to the program.
No tool is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether the centre already writes attitude in the progress note, or only speaks it.
research_questions: Which moments in a session most often drop a client's attitude?

already_counted.description: The greeting, the encouragement and the adjustment stay in b1, b2 and b3.

incremental.description: No tool is added, so there is no upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Attitude is kept in the room with the client, so no hour moves.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Hear which patients supervisors want in the report
Name progress, attitudes and behavior to report
Tell supervisors the patient progress verbally
Draft the written progress note from named points
Check progress, attitudes and behavior in the note
Accept the progress note for the patient dossier
File the accepted progress note in the dossier

tasks.design: The occupational therapy assistant names progress, attitudes and behavior. A template in {OTHER} drafts the written progress note from those points only. She checks every field against the session. The occupational therapist accepts that version, and only then is the accepted note filed in the patient dossier. The template does not record the patient and does not recommend care. The verbal report stays a conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: The written note was free text she composed, and a tool that suggested treatment would be the wrong aid.
tasks.enabler_now: Once she has named progress, attitudes and behavior, a template can draft the note for her check and the therapist's acceptance.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing what the session meant, and telling supervisors verbally, stay with her.
tasks.human_edge: She can see that a tidy note still misstates how the patient behaved.
tasks.altitude: Drafting and filing the written note take less of the report. She still names the points, still speaks to supervisors, and still checks the note. The occupational therapist still accepts it.

reach.task: Accept a progress note into the dossier
reach.learn: Which fields must be present before a note is stored: progress, attitudes and behavior

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a template can place progress, attitude and behavior points the assistant already named into a note. She still checks the meaning. This design does not record the patient.

Fysio.AI records a physiotherapy intake and writes a structured report into the form; the page asks the therapist to check and correct it, and audio is deleted after transcription. The vendor time claim has no study and is not used as a saving. This task only formats points the assistant typed.
A Smartintake AI for occupational therapy is announced and is not yet live, so this design does not depend on it.

In the Netherlands the therapist keeps the dossier, including data needed for good care, for 20 years. A note drafted by an assistant or a tool enters that dossier under the therapist's responsibility, so the occupational therapist accepts the version before it is filed.
In the Netherlands, physiotherapists are BIG-registered and assistants are not, so the assistant does not take the therapist's responsibility for the dossier.
The progress note is health data under GDPR article 9, so a data protection assessment and a processor agreement are required before a template writes into the dossier.
A tool that proposes diagnosis or treatment can fall under medical-device rule 11. This draft only restates the points the assistant listed and does not recommend care.

assumptions: The focal role is the occupational therapy assistant. The occupational therapist owns the treatment plan and accepts the written note.
The structured fields are progress, attitudes and behavior, produced by the assistant in c2. If a field is empty, the draft does not run and she writes the note as today.
Filing the accepted note into the patient dossier is work she does today. The verbal report is a separate conversation and is not shortened.
No audio of the patient or of staff is captured. Upkeep of the three field names is four hours per 100 baseline hours.
The patient dossier is the clinical record in {OTHER}.
unknowns: Whether this centre already has the occupational therapist accept the assistant's note before the dossier stores it.
How often the report is spoken only, with no written note.
research_questions: What share of supervisor reports are written into the dossier rather than spoken only?

already_counted.description: Naming the points, the verbal report and the field check stay in c2, c3 and c5.
The occupational therapist's acceptance of the written note stays in c6.

incremental.description: She keeps the three field names and the rule that an empty field blocks the draft.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When most reports stay verbal, only the written note is drafted and filed, and a thin written share cuts the saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Watch performance during the therapy activities
Judge if the therapy activity is still safe

tasks.design: She watches the patient's performance during therapy activities and encourages in the room. Judging whether the activity is still safe stays with the occupational therapy assistant. No dashboard and no recording are added.
tasks.previous_blocker: Performance is seen in the room, and encouragement is spoken to the patient.
tasks.enabler_now: No enabler watches the movement or supplies the encouragement for her.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding that a movement is unsafe, and finding the right encouragement, stay with her.
tasks.human_edge: She can see fatigue that a later note would miss.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still monitors the activity and encourages the patient.

reach.task: Set up the activity the assistant will monitor
reach.learn: Which setup lets her see the movement without leaving the patient

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: monitoring performance and giving encouragement during therapy are in-person. The digest does not describe a product that watches or encourages a patient.

assumptions: The activity is already chosen in the treatment plan. She monitors and encourages; she does not redesign the activity in this task.
No tool is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether any session is already timed or scored on a form while she watches.
research_questions: Which activities most often need her to stop the patient for safety?

already_counted.description: Watching, the safety judgement and the encouragement stay in d1, d2 and d3.

incremental.description: No tool is added, so there is no upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Monitoring and encouragement stay in the room, so no hour moves.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still instructs families, keeps the client's attitude, and watches performance in the room. Drafting and filing the written progress note take less time. She still names the points, still reports verbally, and still checks the note. The occupational therapist still accepts it into the dossier.
skills_to_grow: Check each progress-note field against the session she watched
Separate progress, attitudes and behavior before a note is drafted
Keep home-program instruction in her own words with the family
role.ambitious_version: A recorder that listens to every session and files a note without her check, or a coach that instructs the family without her, is out of scope. She still teaches, encourages and watches.
